sources.entry: Typebot - Conversational app builder (alternative to Typeform and Landbot). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Typebot is a visual chatbot builder, described as Fair Source, for creating chatbots and embedding them in web or mobile apps while collecting results in real time.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a visual chat builder with 34+ building blocks, including text, image, video, audio and embed bubbles; inputs such as text, email, phone, buttons, picture choice, date picker, payment (Stripe) and file picker; and logic such as conditional branching, redirects, JavaScript scripting and A/B testing. It lists integrations with webhooks/HTTP requests, OpenAI, Google Sheets, Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Zapier, Make.com and Chatwoot. Chatbots can be themed with custom fonts, colors, CSS and reusable templates, and shared via custom domain or as a container, popup or chat bubble using a native JS embed library. Results can be analyzed for drop-off and completion rates and exported to CSV. The README also mentions easy-to-use APIs for developers.
use_cases: build a visual chatbot without coding
embed a chatbot on a website as a popup or chat bubble
collect leads or form-style responses through a conversation
connect chatbot answers to Google Sheets or webhooks
replace Typeform or Landbot style forms
analyze chatbot drop-off and completion rates
how_to_run: Self-hosting instructions are referenced in the README (see the self-hosting installation docs; steps not included in README)
Local development: follow the Local installation section in the Contributing docs
notable: Visual drag-and-drop chatbot builder with 34+ building blocks
Embed library claimed to use no iframe and no external dependencies
Integrations with OpenAI, Google Sheets, Zapier, Make.com and Chatwoot
Results analytics with drop-off rates and CSV export
Reusable theme templates and custom CSS theming
caveats: Licensed under a Functional Source License per the README, not a standard open-source license
Managed cloud service is the officially recommended option; self-hosting is described as an alternative
Some integrations are listed as 'more to come'
